source_text:
Μεγάλης καὶ ἐῤῥωμένης καὶ τελείας ψυχῆς διαγράφει τὸ τέλος,
ὅτι γε ὁ δράκων αὐτῷ, ὥσπερ στρουθίον παραδέδοται παιδίῳ, μηδὲ βλάψαι τὸ
παιδίον δυνάμενον, ὅτι καὶ δεδεμένον αὐτὸ ἄγει ὅπου γε βούλεται τὸ παιδίον καὶ
περιφέρει· οὕτω τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Κυρίου, ὡς στρουθίον ὑποχείριον, ὁ Σατανᾶς
δεδεμένος γεγένηται τοῖς νηπίοις καὶ θηλάζουσιν, ὧν ἐκ στόματος κατηρτήσατο
αἶνον ὁ Θεός. Ἐνσιτοῦνται δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔθνη. Ὥσπερ τῶν πιστῶν βρῶμα ὁ Κύριος,
οὕτως ὁ δράκων τῶν ἀσεβῶν· «Ἔδωκας γὰρ αὐτὸν βρῶμα λαοῖς τοῖς Αἰθίοψι·»
τουτέστι, τοῖς υἱοῖς τοῦ σκότους, τοῖς ἐν ἀγνωσίᾳ. Καθ' ἕκαστον γὰρ λόγον ὃν
παραδεχόμεθα, ἤτοι ἀπὸ τοῦ δράκοντος ἐσθίομεν, ἐὰν παραδεξώμεθα ἀκοὴν ματαίαν, ἢ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐὰν παραδεξώμεθα λόγον οἰκοδομοῦντα καὶ ὠφελοῦντα.
Πᾶν δὲ πλωτὸν συνελθὸν οὐ μὴ ἐνέγκωσι βύρσαν μίαν οὐρᾶς αὐτοῦ. Σαφέστερον δὲ
εἰπεῖν· Οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οἱ πλοίοις τοῖς σώμασι χρώμενοι, τὰ τελευταῖα τοῦ δράκοντος
καὶ τὰ ἔσχατα νεκρῶσαι αὐτοὶ καθ' ἑαυτοὺς οὐ δύνανται· θείας δὲ δυνάμεως ἐπισκοπούσης, καὶ ὅλον αὐτὸν κομίσαι καὶ νεκρῶσαι δυνάμεθα. Νεκροῦμεν δὲ ἕκαστος, τὸ
ὅσον ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ, τὸν διάβολον, κατὰ τό· «Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς συντρίψει τὸν σατανᾶν ὑπὸ τοὺς
πόδας ὑμῶν ἐν τάχει.» Εἰς πτύξιν θώρακος αὐτοῦ τίς ἂν εἰσέλθοι, Θώραξ καὶ στῆθος
ὀνομάζεται, ὅπου ἐστὶ τὸ ἡγεμονικόν. Οὐχ ἁπλοῦς ἐστιν ὁ θώραξ αὐτοῦ· δόλιός
ἐστιν, ἐπτυγμένος ἐστίν· ἅγιος δὲ ἐλέγχειν αὐτὸν δύναται, καὶ δεῖξαι, ὅτι ἔπτυκται·
τῷ γὰρ ἁγίῳ οὐκ ἔπτυκται. Πνεῦμα δὲ οὐ μὴ διέλθῃ αὐτόν. Τὸ, «οὐ μὴ διέλθῃ,» οὐχ
ὅτι οὐ διέρχεται καὶ παρέρχεται, ἀλλ' ὅτι οὐδὲν αὐτὸν λανθάνει· πάντας δεῖ δι'
αὐτοῦ ἐλθεῖν. Ἑαυτοὺς οὖν παρασκευάσωμεν, τοῦ μὴ κατασχεθῆναι ὑπ' αὐτοῦ. Οἱ δὲ
ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ εἶδος Ἑωσφόρου.
thought_title: The dragon bound and given as food; the saint examines the dragon's folds; the dragon's eyes imitate the morning star
orientation: Origen continues interpreting Job 41, showing how the dragon (Satan) is delivered bound like a sparrow to simple believers, becomes food for the ungodly, and is mortified by divine power; he then examines the dragon's folded breast as the seat of deceit and notes that no spirit passes through him unperceived, ending with the dragon's eyes having the appearance of the morning star.
pass_a_gloss: The end of a great and strong and perfect soul is described, because the dragon has been delivered to him like a sparrow to a child, not being able even to harm the child, because even bound it leads it wherever the child wishes and carries it around; so by the grace of the Lord, like a sparrow in hand, Satan has become bound to infants and those nursing, out of whose mouth God has prepared praise. Nations are fed in him. As the Lord is food for the faithful, so the dragon is food for the impious; 'For you gave him as food to the peoples, the Ethiopians'; that is, to the sons of darkness, those in ignorance. For according to each word which we receive, either we eat from the dragon, if we accept a vain hearing, or from Christ, if we accept a word building up and benefiting. Every floating thing coming together shall not bear one skin of his tail. More clearly to say: Men, using ships as bodies, are not able by themselves to deaden the last parts of the dragon and the extremes; but divine power overseeing, we are able to bring the whole of him and deaden him. And each of us deadens the devil, as far as lies in him, according to 'And God will crush Satan under your feet quickly.' Into a fold of his breast who would enter? Breast and chest is named where the ruling part is. His breast is not simple; it is deceitful, it is folded; a holy man is able to examine it and show that it is folded; for to the holy man it is not folded. And a spirit shall not pass through him. The 'shall not pass through' does not mean that it does not go through and pass by, but that nothing escapes his notice; all must go through him. Let us therefore prepare ourselves, lest we be seized by him. And his eyes are the appearance of the morning star.

choices.why: Matches the brief's glossary 'sparrow' for στρουθίον in this passage; a small bird used as a pet or plaything, emphasizing the dragon's helplessness.
Uses the glossary senses for νήπιος and θηλάζω; keeps the two groups distinct as in the Greek.
Literal rendering of the metaphor; the text says men use ships as bodies, not that bodies are ships.
Glossary 'breast' for θώραξ; 'fold' for πτύξ; the breast is the seat of the ruling part.

choices.term: Πνεῦμα δὲ οὐ μὴ διέλθῃ αὐτόν
choices.english: And a spirit shall not pass through him
choices.why: Keeps the future indicative force of οὐ μὴ + aorist subjunctive as a strong denial; the next clause explains the sense.
rejected: No spirit will pass through him
A spirit will not pass through him unnoticed

choices.why: Glossary 'morning star' for Ἑωσφόρος; εἶδος is 'appearance' not the thing itself.

bible_refs.note: Will you play with him as with a bird, or bind him as a sparrow for a child?
out of whose mouth God has prepared praise
you gave him as food to the peoples, the Ethiopians
And God will crush Satan under your feet quickly

pass_b_english: It describes the end of a great, strong, and perfect soul, because the dragon has been handed over to him like a sparrow to a child, unable even to harm the child, since the child can lead it bound wherever he wishes and carry it about; so by the Lord's grace Satan has become bound like a sparrow in the hands of infants and sucklings, from whose mouth God has prepared praise (Psalm 8:2). Nations are fed on him. Just as the Lord is food for the faithful, so the dragon is food for the ungodly; 'You gave him as food to the peoples, the Ethiopians' (Psalm 74:14)—that is, to the children of darkness, to those in ignorance. For with every word we receive, we either eat from the dragon if we accept a vain hearing, or from Christ if we accept a word that builds up and benefits.

No ship, though they gather together, will ever bear one hide of his tail. To speak more plainly: human beings, who use their bodies as ships, cannot by themselves mortify the tail of the dragon and its final parts; but with divine power overseeing, we can bring the whole of him and mortify it. Each of us mortifies the devil, so far as lies in himself, according to the word: 'And God will crush Satan under your feet quickly' (Romans 16:20). Who would enter a fold of his breast? The breast and the chest are named as the place where the ruling part is. His breast is not simple; it is deceitful, it is folded. A holy person can convict him and show that it is folded; for to the holy one it is not folded. And a spirit shall not pass through him. The words 'shall not pass through' do not mean that it does not go through and pass by, but that nothing escapes him; all must come through him. Let us therefore prepare ourselves, so as not to be seized by him. His eyes have the appearance of the morning star.

problems.quote: human beings, who use ships as bodies,
problems.source_quote: Οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οἱ πλοίοις τοῖς σώμασι χρώμενοι,
problems.why: Object and predicate are reversed: articular τοῖς σώμασι is what is used, and anarthrous πλοίοις is 'as ships'.
problems.fix: human beings, who use their bodies as ships,

problems.quote: No floating thing gathering together will ever bear one hide of his tail.
problems.source_quote: Πᾶν δὲ πλωτὸν συνελθὸν οὐ μὴ ἐνέγκωσι βύρσαν μίαν οὐρᾶς αὐτοῦ.
problems.why: πλωτόν is a ship, the image the next clause allegorizes, not a vague floating thing.
problems.fix: No ship, though they gather together, will ever carry off one hide of his tail.
problems.ruling: πλωτὸν means sailing vessel/ship, directly picked up by πλοίοις next; 'No floating thing' obscures the image and breaks the exegetical link.

problems.quote: The end describes a great, strong, and perfect soul,
problems.source_quote: Μεγάλης καὶ ἐῤῥωμένης καὶ τελείας ψυχῆς διαγράφει τὸ τέλος,
problems.why: Subject and object are reversed: 'the end' (τὸ τέλος) is the object of 'describes', and the genitive 'of a great, strong, and perfect soul' modifies it.
problems.fix: It describes the end of a great, strong, and perfect soul,
problems.ruling: διαγράφει takes τὸ τέλος as object; genitive ψυχῆς modifies τέλος, so the soul’s end is described, not the reverse.

edits.old: The end describes a great, strong, and perfect soul,
edits.new: It describes the end of a great, strong, and perfect soul,

edits.old: No floating thing gathering together will ever bear one hide of his tail.
edits.new: No ship, though they gather together, will ever bear one hide of his tail.

edits.old: human beings, who use ships as bodies,
edits.new: human beings, who use their bodies as ships,

fixed: Agency: τὸ τέλος is object of διαγράφει modified by Μεγάλης...ψυχῆς — changed to 'It describes the end of...'.
Mistranslation: πλωτὸν is a ship/vessel as next clause allegorizes — changed 'floating thing' to 'ship' with plural verb retained as 'though they gather together'.
Mistranslation: τοῖς σώμασι is the thing used, πλοίοις the predicate — changed to 'use their bodies as ships'.

problems.source_quote: «Ἔδωκας γὰρ αὐτὸν βρῶμα λαοῖς τοῖς Αἰθίοψι·»
problems.why: Uses Hebrew numbering instead of the required LXX Psalm numbering; in the LXX this verse (with 'Ethiopians') is Psalm 73:14, whereas Psalm 74 is a different psalm.
In this Psalm 8 echo, θηλάζοντες are suckling infants, while “those nursing” means people who nurse them.
problems.fix: infants and sucklings, from whose mouth God has prepared praise (Psalm 8:3)
problems.ruling: In Ps 8:2, θηλάζουσιν means suckling babies, not mothers; "infants and those nursing" misleads readers into picturing nursing mothers.

edits.old: infants and those nursing, from whose mouth God has prepared praise (Psalm 8:2)
edits.new: infants and sucklings, from whose mouth God has prepared praise (Psalm 8:3)

fixed: wrong_scripture real: «Ἔδωκας γὰρ αὐτὸν βρῶμα λαοῖς τοῖς Αἰθίοψι» is LXX Psalm 73:14, fixed to (Psalm 73:14)
mistranslation real: τοῖς νηπίοις καὶ θηλάζουσιν echoes Psalm 8 suckling infants, not nurses; fixed to infants and sucklings with LXX (Psalm 8:3)

last_rejected.source_quote: ὧν ἐκ στόματος κατηρτήσατο αἶνον ὁ Θεός
last_rejected.why: Those words are Psalm 8:2 in a standard English Bible; 8:3 is the heavens verse. Psalm 8's number does not differ in the LXX.
last_rejected.fix: from whose mouth God has prepared praise (Psalm 8:2).
last_rejected.ruling: In LXX versification, "νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων... κατηρτήσατο αἶνον" is Psalm 8:3 (superscription is 8:1), consistent with LXX numbering in Psalm 73:14.
